description:
We are students at Tuwaiq Technical Gifted Schools, passionate about tech and innovation. Excited to join NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to gain hands-on experience and create impactful solutions.

we want to learn together, explore our potential, and bring great ideas to life!
summary: Beyond Earth is a web game that trains kids as junior astronauts using real NASA data. Players pick an astronaut, walk around an interactive spaceship, explore real planets through the ship’s window, and land to study them. On rocky worlds they build a working colony, where NASA data sets the rules: sunlight decides how much power solar panels produce, ice decides whether they can get water, temperature decides how much heating they need, and live solar flare alerts decide how much radiation shielding they need. At the end, the player discovers the twist: the best planet for life is Earth, and the skills they learned in space are the same skills that protect it.
details:
• What it does: a kid-friendly game made of a main menu, an age check, an AI-free helper cat that reads text aloud and points at buttons (required for players under 10), five astronaut characters, a cinematic intro, a walkable spaceship, planet studies, and colony building.
  • How it works: Python (Streamlit) fetches NASA data and passes it to an HTML/JavaScript game. Planets are studied in different ways: on rocky planets, the player tests gravity by jumping; on gas giants, they float with no ground to stand on, and on Venus they send a probe before it melts.
  • Data-driven gameplay: jump height = Earth jump ÷ real gravity. Solar output = real sunlight received. We calculated the Earth Similarity Index (Schulze-Makuch et al., 2011) ourselves from NASA values and turned it into star ratings kids understand.
  • Benefits: kids learn about habitability, resource management, radiation and the human body in space by playing, not memorizing. It also builds respect for Earth through daily real-life “Earth missions”.
  • Tools: Python, Streamlit, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, GitHub.
